title: Historic Home Restoration in Westchester NY: Preserving Character While Building for Today
excerpt: Restoring a historic Westchester home takes more than good intentions. It takes someone who understands both the bones of an old house and the demands of modern building codes.
content:
Westchester County is full of homes with real history. Walk through neighborhoods in Scarsdale, Bronxville, and Larchmont and you'll see Victorian porches, colonial details, Arts and Crafts millwork, and brick chimneys that have stood for over a century. These homes have character that new construction can't replicate. But they also have problems that new construction doesn't have to solve.

Historic home restoration is not the same as a standard renovation. It's not about ripping out what's old and putting in what's new. It's about understanding what you're looking at, respecting what works, fixing what doesn't, and knowing how to do all of that while keeping your house intact and your local building department satisfied.

Why Historic Homes Need Someone Who Knows What They're Doing

A lot of homeowners in towns like Mamaroneck, Pelham, and Rye come to us with homes that have been modified over the decades. A wall removed in the 1970s. A bathroom added in the 1990s. A roof that's been patched too many times. Sometimes the work was done without permits. Sometimes it was done without regard for how the house was originally built.

The problem shows up when you try to make the next change. You can't just assume the walls are load-bearing where you think they are. You can't skip the permits because someone else did decades ago. You need a licensed architect in Westchester, NY who can read old construction, understand what's really happening inside those walls, and plan work that actually complies with current codes.

Design-Build Makes Restoration Smoother

We operate as a design-build firm in Westchester, which means Silvio Luca handles both the architectural planning and the actual construction. He's a licensed New York State architect and a licensed general contractor. He runs every project personally. That matters in historic work because the architect and the contractor need to be talking constantly. Details matter. Solutions that look good on paper need to actually work in the field.

In homes throughout Tuckahoe, Eastchester, and White Plains, we've handled restorations that involve everything from foundation work to roof restoration to bringing old electrical and plumbing systems up to code. Each municipality has its own building department and permit process, and we know how to work within all of them. That's what happens when you serve the entire county for years.

Keeping Character While Living Comfortably

Historic home restoration doesn't mean you have to live like it's 1910. You can have modern kitchens and bathrooms. You can open up floor plans where it makes sense. You can add second stories or primary suite additions in Hastings-on-Hudson or Tarrytown without destroying the architectural integrity of the original structure.

The key is knowing what to keep, what to restore, and what to upgrade thoughtfully. That takes experience and a real understanding of both old houses and new requirements.
